rationale: Evidence from the development simulator (entityR2A, iteration 0): the oval finished in 75% of trials (mean 1.91 s), but the s-bend and slalom ended off track in every trial, at progress 0.29 and 0.12. The off-track limit is max(0.06 m, 0.0125 + body_width/4) = 0.06 m for this body, and max_error on the failing tracks was about 0.061 to 0.062 m, so the robot is leaving the tape at the first sharp bend. Line-loss events averaged about 1.05 on those tracks, which means the line is lost during the bend and last_direction does not bring it back. Steering oscillation is low (0.15 to 0.21), so the problem is not jitter. The response is too weak and too late for the tighter curves. Changes: (1) raise kp from 2.5 to 3.5 so the robot corrects harder for a given offset; (2) raise kd from 0.3 to 0.6 to damp the stronger correction and limit overshoot; (3) lower base_speed from 1.4 to 1.3, a smaller cut than the Evaluator's 1.2 suggestion, because 1.2 would probably leave the average speed too low to finish the 3.0 s limit (about 1.5 m/s is needed). Geometry and sensor weights are unchanged so the controller effect can be isolated, and ki stays at 0 because no one-sided offset is visible in the data. Expected result: fewer off-track exits on the s-bend and slalom, with max_error below 0.06 and at least one completed slalom or s-bend run; finish time should stay under 3 s on the oval (about 2.0 s). Risk: kp 3.5 with kd 0.6 may cause oscillation on straights. Hypotheses to test: (a) the slalom fails because of too little steering authority, so higher kp should raise progress; (b) base_speed 1.3 still gives finish times under 3 s. Measurements requested: all metrics, so I can see the per-track max_error, line_loss_events and completion_time trade-off.
